text: Not all men, not all men. Okay, hire a male babysitter then. To be alone with your children, in charge of your children. So let me translate what she's doing here. In a lot of feminist slash woke spaces, it is popular to throw out broad claims like men are abusers, men are predators, men are oppressors. And when someone counters with not all men, her comeback here is basically, okay then, hire a male babysitter and leave him alone with your kids. And yeah, emotionally that sounds like a slam dunk, but logically it falls apart the moment you slow it down. First, it is true that most babysitters are women, but that's not proof that men are uniquely dangerous. It is mostly proof that far fewer men work in childcare in the first place. If 90% of babysitters are women, then most people will hire women simply because that's who is available. Second, when parents hire a babysitter, they don't hire based on man versus woman. They hire based on trust signals, experience, references, reviews, background checks, and recommendations from friends. That's the whole point of hiring someone to watch your child. You don't just spin a roulette wheel and pick a random stranger. So if you meet a male babysitter with strong references, verified experience, and good reviews, plenty of parents would hire him. The same way, plenty of parents are fine with male teachers, male doctors, male coaches, male family friends, and male relatives being around their kids. Now let's flip the scenario. Imagine you're hiring security or a bodyguard. Statistically, you'll see more men in that industry. That doesn't mean all women are weak and they are cowards. No, it means the labor market is gender skewed. And the decision usually comes down to credentials, training, background, recommendations, experience. If you find a woman with strong credentials, a lot of people would hire her too. Same logic applies to babysitting. So no, the reason male babysitters are rare isn't automatically because men are abusers and predators. A much more realistic reason is social norms and stereotypes. People assume women are more nurturing. Men are less interested in childcare. Men get discouraged from entering that space. And yes, some parents might feel uncomfortable because society has trained them to be suspicious. But that's not the same thing as men are abusers and predators by nature. Same way, having fewer women in military or security does not mean women are traitors and cowards by nature. So next time, instead of using childcare as a cheap trap to push an ideology, how about we use some adult logic? Judge individuals by evidence and behavior. Acknowledge real risk without demonizing half the population. And stop pretending that emotional punchlines are the same thing as truth. Because hire a male babysitter then is not a logical argument. It is a viral slogan to push your narrative.
